bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Customer concentration — MD&A Risk Management lists this first among operational risks: a significant portion of revenue continues to be derived from key customers, even though the Company enjoys long-standing relationships with leading global FMCG companies. Mitigation is structural rather than contractual — broadening into Beauty & Cosmetics and other Personal Care categories, engaging regional and emerging brands, and widening the customer base across geographies and end-use segments.
- Raw material availability and cost, particularly polymers — Availability and pricing of key raw materials, particularly polymers, remain influenced by crude oil prices, supply-demand dynamics and global logistics. Managed through strategic supplier partnerships, multi-source procurement, disciplined inventory management, productivity initiatives and commercial actions.
- Geopolitical and trade / tariff risk across a global manufacturing network — Ongoing geopolitical conflicts, evolving trade policies and tariff-related developments have increased uncertainty across global supply chains. The MD&A Outlook specifically names the ongoing conflict in the Middle East alongside evolving trade policies as a continuing challenge to supply chains and input costs. The diversified network of more than 21 facilities in 11 countries is the stated mitigation.
- Macroeconomic volatility affecting demand and input costs — Inflationary pressures, foreign exchange fluctuations, changing consumer demand and slower economic growth across key markets could impact demand for packaged products and influence input costs; addressed through disciplined pricing, cost management and capital allocation.
- Climate and sustainability regulation, and the constrained supply of recycled input materials — Two linked disclosures. The MD&A flags increasing regulatory focus on sustainability and Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations reshaping the industry. The BRSR material-issues table goes further: 'Materials' is the only item classified as a Risk (all other material issues are Opportunities), with limited availability of recycled materials, supplier-level innovation gaps and gradual customer adoption slowing the transition — and its financial implication is stated as Negative, with higher costs linked to recycled materials named as the challenge.
- Competitive and market dynamics requiring continuous reinvestment — Consumer preferences, packaging formats and customer requirements have evolved rapidly, particularly in Beauty & Cosmetics and sustainable packaging. Maintaining leadership requires continuous investment in innovation, differentiated products, commercial capabilities and manufacturing technologies — i.e. the moat is reinvestment-dependent rather than self-sustaining.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy as digital capability deepens — Named as a key priority as EPL strengthens its digital capabilities; managed through an information security framework supported by ISO 27001 standards, regular risk assessments, employee awareness programmes and continued cybersecurity investment.
- Workplace safety across a manufacturing base, with FY26 deterioration — The health & safety tables in this bundle show a step-up in FY 2025-26: one fatality in the permanent-employee series (fatality rate 0.0186) and one in the contractual series (fatality rate 0.0118), against zero fatalities in each of the preceding four years. Permanent-employee LTIFR rose to 0.35 from 0.07, lost days to 110 from 0, and total work-related accidents to 102 from 4. All operational sites are ISO 45001 certified (certificates issued December 2024, valid until December 2027) and mitigation runs through engineering and administrative controls, monthly Safety Committee meetings and the EPL Risk and Incident Management System.

outlook.body:
- The 4X4 framework is the organising strategy: four pillars — Category, Customers, Country and Cost — supported by four enablers — Innovation, Agile Sales & Marketing, Digital Transformation and One EPL Culture.
- Category: hold leadership in Oral Care while accelerating faster-growing categories, above all Beauty & Cosmetics, through an expanded extruded tube portfolio, Neo Seam technology and other value-added packaging solutions; Personal Care & Beyond now accounts for 53% of tube revenue.
- Customers: widen the base beyond large global accounts towards regional and emerging Beauty & Cosmetics brands, backed by investment in front-end commercial capability, commercial agility and customer service so smaller and mid-sized customers can be served economically.
- Country: expand in high-growth geographies that align with customers' own growth ambitions — the Thailand facility was commissioned in FY26 and Brazil continued its ramp-up, taking the network to more than 21 facilities across 11 countries and letting EPL manufacture close to customers while strengthening supply chain resilience.
- Cost: disciplined operational excellence and cost optimisation across procurement, manufacturing and overheads, with productivity initiatives and operating leverage funding continued investment behind growth.
- Build a diversified consumer packaging platform for emerging markets through the proposed merger with Indovida India Private Limited, combining EPL's leadership in specialty flexible packaging with Indovida's rigid packaging presence to broaden product portfolio, customer coverage and geographic footprint; EPL continues as the listed entity.
- People strategy anchored on organisation structures enabling growth, capability building, culture and engagement, diversity and inclusion, and talent development — carried by Ugrow, Yantrashala technical assessments, Individual and Career Development Plans and regional Leadership Academies in Europe, India and China.
- Diversity, equity and inclusion as an operating discipline rather than a statement: gender-neutral job descriptions, diverse interview panels, bias-checked selection, and an explicit shift of attention from headline female representation (already past its 32% mark) to women's representation in leadership roles and a steady diverse talent pipeline.
- Internal mobility as the leadership pipeline: 144 employees promoted through a structured merit-based process in FY 2025-26 and 42 employees from India taking up roles in Poland, Germany, the US, Brazil, Mexico and Egypt.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 expansion was carried by two greenfield sites and one large inorganic step. On the organic side, the Board's Report records that during the year the Company invested a further amount of ~` 30 Crore in EPL Packaging (Thailand) Co. Ltd. to support operations in the first year of its incorporation including commissioning of its manufacturing facility, and invested ` 150 Crore in EPL Brasil LTDA, which is expected to have a favourable impact on its financial position. The Value Creation Model describes the same programme as 21 global manufacturing facilities, new capacity added in Brazil and a greenfield expansion initiated in Thailand. Product-side capacity was widened too: the Managing Director's letter states the Company expanded its product portfolio and capabilities by investing in extruded tube capabilities, creating a new product platform that enables it to serve new customers, alongside applicator, dispensing, digital and specialty printing capability and NEOSeam. The MD&A frames the forward runway as further expansion across Southeast Asia, Latin America and other attractive growth markets, with higher capacity utilisation named as one of the levers for future margin gain. The largest announced expansion is inorganic: the proposed merger with Indovida India Private Limited, announced in March 2026, a scheme of amalgamation combining EPL's laminated and tube packaging with Indovida's scale in rigid PET packaging, under which EPL remains the listed entity. The combined business is expected to generate annual revenues of ~US$1 billion with nearly 75% of revenues derived from emerging markets; on completion Indorama Ventures is expected to become a co-promoter with a ~51.8% shareholding while Blackstone will hold ~16.6%. Indovida is described as a net-cash business, and management expects the combination to be earnings accretive and to expand the platform particularly across South-east Asia and Africa, subject to shareholder, regulatory and judicial approvals. outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The global packaging industry is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 3-4% over the next five years (Mordor Intelligence), supported by rising consumption across personal care, pharmaceuticals, food and home care, increasing urbanisation and the expansion of organised retail and e-commerce.
- Sustainability is described as the most significant structural trend shaping the industry: the global sustainable packaging market is estimated to grow at a CAGR of approximately 7-8%, significantly outpacing the broader packaging industry.
- Regulatory focus on recyclability, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks and brand commitments towards circular packaging are accelerating adoption of recyclable, mono-material and post-consumer recycled solutions.
- Flexible packaging continues to outpace overall market growth, driven by lower material consumption, a reduced carbon footprint and greater design flexibility.
- Beauty & Cosmetics carries strong momentum as brands seek premium, aesthetically differentiated and sustainable packaging — a trend management explicitly maps onto its own strategic focus.
- Customers increasingly value partners that can combine innovation, global manufacturing capability and reliable supply with local responsiveness, which management positions as EPL's structural advantage.
- Demand resilience comes from essential categories — Oral Care, Pharmaceuticals and Food — while premiumisation and innovation reshape requirements and open categories like Beauty and Cosmetics.
- Macro backdrop: global GDP growth of approximately 3.3% in calendar 2025, with the IMF revising its 2026 global forecast to approximately 3.1% on Middle East geopolitical tension, higher energy prices, supply chain disruption and tighter financial conditions.
- Regional macro divergence: India the fastest-growing major economy at a projected 6.3-6.5% with improving consumption and rural recovery; China resilient at around 4.4-4.5% on policy support; Europe a subdued recovery amid weak industrial activity.
- Energy and logistics cost pressure is expected to be more pronounced across the Middle East and other energy-importing emerging economies.
- Mix and operating leverage are the stated margin levers — a favourable product mix led by higher-value Beauty & Cosmetics, volume-driven operating leverage, disciplined cost management and productivity initiatives held EBITDA margin above 20% for seven consecutive quarters.
- Regional performance is uneven and management says so: Americas strongest (revenue +~21.1%, EBITDA +~37.1%) having absorbed the evolving US tariff environment through local manufacturing; EAP +~15.7% with the Thailand commissioning; AMESA +~5.1%; Europe grew ~10.4% but EBITDA fell ~3.2% to a ~14.5% margin, with only a gradual improvement expected over the medium term.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: A specialty packaging company making multilayer collapsible laminated and plastic tubes for Beauty & Cosmetics, Oral Care, Pharma & Health, Food & Nutrition and Home Care brands, from a manufacturing network spanning 11 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: EPL manufactures plastic packaging materials — principally multilayer collapsible laminated tubes, extruded plastic tubes and laminates — which account for 94.70% of the standalone entity's turnover under NIC code 22203. Its customers are international, regional and local niche consumer brands across Beauty & Cosmetics, Oral Care, Food & Nutrition, Pharma & Health and Home Care, served from a global network of 21 manufacturing facilities across 11 countries organised into four regions (AMESA, EAP, Americas and Europe). The business is deliberately shifting mix away from its traditional Oral Care base: Personal Care & Beyond now accounts for 53% of tube revenue, and recyclable formats reached 39% of tube sales in FY26.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- The global packaging industry is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 3-4% over the next five years (Mordor Intelligence), supported by rising consumption across personal care, pharmaceuticals, food and home care, increasing urbanisation and the expansion of organised retail and e-commerce.
- Sustainability is described as the most significant structural trend shaping the industry: the global sustainable packaging market is estimated to grow at a CAGR of approximately 7-8%, significantly outpacing the broader packaging industry.
- Regulatory focus on recyclability, Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) frameworks and brand commitments towards circular packaging are accelerating adoption of recyclable, mono-material and post-consumer recycled solutions.
- Flexible packaging continues to outpace overall market growth, driven by lower material consumption, a reduced carbon footprint and greater design flexibility.
- Beauty & Cosmetics carries strong momentum as brands seek premium, aesthetically differentiated and sustainable packaging — a trend management explicitly maps onto its own strategic focus.
- Customers increasingly value partners that can combine innovation, global manufacturing capability and reliable supply with local responsiveness, which management positions as EPL's structural advantage.
- Demand resilience comes from essential categories — Oral Care, Pharmaceuticals and Food — while premiumisation and innovation reshape requirements and open categories like Beauty and Cosmetics.
- Macro backdrop: global GDP growth of approximately 3.3% in calendar 2025, with the IMF revising its 2026 global forecast to approximately 3.1% on Middle East geopolitical tension, higher energy prices, supply chain disruption and tighter financial conditions.
- Regional macro divergence: India the fastest-growing major economy at a projected 6.3-6.5% with improving consumption and rural recovery; China resilient at around 4.4-4.5% on policy support; Europe a subdued recovery amid weak industrial activity.
- Energy and logistics cost pressure is expected to be more pronounced across the Middle East and other energy-importing emerging economies.
- Mix and operating leverage are the stated margin levers — a favourable product mix led by higher-value Beauty & Cosmetics, volume-driven operating leverage, disciplined cost management and productivity initiatives held EBITDA margin above 20% for seven consecutive quarters.
- Regional performance is uneven and management says so: Americas strongest (revenue +~21.1%, EBITDA +~37.1%) having absorbed the evolving US tariff environment through local manufacturing; EAP +~15.7% with the Thailand commissioning; AMESA +~5.1%; Europe grew ~10.4% but EBITDA fell ~3.2% to a ~14.5% margin, with only a gradual improvement expected over the medium term.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 expansion was carried by two greenfield sites and one large inorganic step. On the organic side, the Board's Report records that during the year the Company invested a further amount of ~` 30 Crore in EPL Packaging (Thailand) Co. Ltd. to support operations in the first year of its incorporation including commissioning of its manufacturing facility, and invested ` 150 Crore in EPL Brasil LTDA, which is expected to have a favourable impact on its financial position. The Value Creation Model describes the same programme as 21 global manufacturing facilities, new capacity added in Brazil and a greenfield expansion initiated in Thailand. Product-side capacity was widened too: the Managing Director's letter states the Company expanded its product portfolio and capabilities by investing in extruded tube capabilities, creating a new product platform that enables it to serve new customers, alongside applicator, dispensing, digital and specialty printing capability and NEOSeam. The MD&A frames the forward runway as further expansion across Southeast Asia, Latin America and other attractive growth markets, with higher capacity utilisation named as one of the levers for future margin gain. The largest announced expansion is inorganic: the proposed merger with Indovida India Private Limited, announced in March 2026, a scheme of amalgamation combining EPL's laminated and tube packaging with Indovida's scale in rigid PET packaging, under which EPL remains the listed entity. The combined business is expected to generate annual revenues of ~US$1 billion with nearly 75% of revenues derived from emerging markets; on completion Indorama Ventures is expected to become a co-promoter with a ~51.8% shareholding while Blackstone will hold ~16.6%. Indovida is described as a net-cash business, and management expects the combination to be earnings accretive and to expand the platform particularly across South-east Asia and Africa, subject to shareholder, regulatory and judicial approvals. No rupee capex quantum is usable from this bundle — see capex_disclosed.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Scale and proximity: a diversified network of more than 21 facilities across 11 countries lets EPL manufacture regionally and serve customers close to their markets, which is also the stated defence against tariff and trade disruption — the Americas navigated the evolving US tariff environment without compromising profitability and in fact expanded margin
- Patent-backed innovation: 27 patents secured during FY26 taking the global portfolio to 154 granted patents as on March 31, 2026, plus 23 further applications filed and 2 design patents filed in Europe; the Creativity & Innovation Lab co-creates with customers from concept through commercialisation
- Sustainability as a commercial moat, not just compliance: EcoVadis Platinum (top 1% globally), recyclable tubes at 39% of tube sales up from 33% in FY25, and Platina / r-Platina meeting the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) — the AR states sustainability has evolved from a compliance imperative into a source of competitive advantage
- Long-standing relationships with leading global and regional FMCG brands built over four decades, with switching friction reinforced by co-developed, brand-specific packaging
- Mix upgrade under way: Beauty & Cosmetics grew approximately 30% in FY26 and Personal Care & Beyond now accounts for 53% of tube revenue, reducing dependence on the traditional Oral Care base
- Cost discipline and operating leverage that sustained EBITDA margins above 20% for seven consecutive quarters
- One EPL culture and a global-yet-local operating model that allows best practices to be scaled across regions while remaining locally agile
